about.title: A refuge between rock and cloud forest
about.p1: Camping El Higuerón is located in the mountains of Choachí, surrounded by high Andean forest and rock formations that bring the Bendito Sea climbing sector to life. It is a space for those seeking to disconnect from the city and reconnect with what matters.
about.p2: Here there is no city noise or unnecessary distractions. Only the sound of the wind, the birds, and the fire at night. A place to camp, climb, and live the mountain in a simple, real, and close way.

boulder.description: A boulder area with different difficulty levels. Low-height climbing without a rope, ideal for training strength and technique.

safety.title: Safety Recommendations
safety.intro: Climbing is a risky activity. Although the sector is equipped and maintained, every climber must take responsibility for their own safety and that of their partners.
tips: Always climb with a trusted partner
Check your gear before every attempt
Know your limits and don't exceed them
Always wear a helmet in the climbing area
Respect the site guidelines

intro.title: Outdoor bouldering
intro.p1: The boulder area at Camping El Higuerón offers a unique bouldering experience. Surrounded by high Andean forest, you'll find diverse problems on natural rock that will challenge your technique, strength, and creativity.
intro.p2: Boulder is a discipline that allows more direct contact with the rock, without ropes or harnesses, where every move counts and reading the problem is essential for success.

levels.title: Problems by level
levels.subtitle: Classification using the V scale (Hueco Scale), the most widely used for boulder in Colombia and Latin America.

v0.description: Basic problems ideal for learning the discipline and developing technique.

v2.description: Greater complexity in moves and better fitness required.

v4.description: Technical problems that require strength and reading moves.

v6.description: Demanding challenges for climbers with boulder experience.

crashpads.title: Using Crashpads
crashpads.p1: Crashpads are special mats designed to cushion falls while bouldering. They are essential for practicing safely.
crashpads.p2: Check crashpad availability in our gear section. If you bring your own, make sure to place it correctly for the landing zone of the problem you're working.
tips: Always use crashpads to protect falls
Practice with a spotter to help guide falls
Check the landing zone before every attempt
Warm up properly before trying hard problems
Know your limits and rest when needed

intro.title: Camping in nature
intro.p1: Camping El Higuerón offers a place to camp in a calm, safe setting, surrounded by the nature of the high Andean forest. Here you can disconnect from the modern world and reconnect with what is essential.
intro.p2: Whether you come to climb, boulder, or simply enjoy the mountain, our campground is the perfect place to spend the night and wake up to the sounds of the forest.

location.title: How to get here?
location.intro: Camping El Higuerón is located in the mountains of Choachí, within the high Andean forest ecosystem. As a rural mountain area, it's important to plan your arrival in advance.
items: Bogotá - Choachí road Pr 6+100 Route 4006A km 23
Some areas have limited cell signal
Coordinate your arrival in advance to receive clear, up-to-date directions

variable.description: Cold climate. Mountain weather can change quickly. Be ready for sun, rain, and cold in the same day. Average temperature 15°C

intro.title: The High Andean Forest
intro.p1: Camping El Higuerón is located in the mountains of Choachí, within the high Andean forest ecosystem. A setting of mist, humidity, and dense vegetation, where the mountain is lived directly and without intermediaries.
intro.p2: Here the landscape is not only visual: you feel it. The wind through the trees, the birdsong, and the silence of the night create an atmosphere that constantly changes and invites you to adapt to the natural rhythm of the place.
intro.p3: It is a space to disconnect from the urban, breathe cold mountain air, and inhabit the surroundings as they are: simple, alive, and authentic.
intro.imageAlt: View of the high Andean forest

characteristics.title: Place characteristics
characteristics.subtitle: A privileged natural setting for adventure and rest

altitude.title: Altitude
altitude.description: Located in a mountain area within the high Andean forest at 3050 masl

climate.title: Cold Climate
climate.description: Cool days with constant changes and cold nights.

air.title: Clean Air
air.description: Clean air, high humidity, and direct contact with the forest.

floraFauna.subtitle: Discover the biodiversity of the ecosystem

birds.title: Native Birds
birds.description: Presence of hummingbirds, tanagers, woodpeckers, and other species native to the forest.

vegetation.title: Vegetation
vegetation.description: Bromeliads, mosses, ferns, orchids, and high-mountain vegetation.

forest.title: Andean Forest
forest.description: Siete cueros, gaques, higuerones, and other species that form a dense, humid ecosystem

connection.title: Connection with the surroundings
connection.p1: At El Higuerón there is no rush. Time changes pace and the experience becomes simpler: walking, climbing, observing, or simply being.
connection.p2: Whether climbing, walking the trails, or simply sitting by the campfire, you'll feel how the mountain recharges you with energy and calm.

hero.title: Muro Bendito Sea
hero.subtitle: A natural crag with 15 equipped routes for sport climbing

intro.title: Bendito Sea: Climbing on natural rock
intro.p1: Bendito Sea is an impressive natural rock formation in the heart of Camping El Higuerón. This crag offers an authentic sport climbing experience.
intro.p2: With 15 climbing routes already equipped with bolted anchors, the Bendito Sea wall is an ideal destination for both beginners and those seeking more demanding challenges. Each route offers unique features that let you develop and test your skills.
intro.imageAlt: View of the Bendito Sea wall

features.title: Wall features
features.subtitle: Everything that makes Bendito Sea special

rock.title: Natural Rock
rock.description: A natural crag with unique formations perfect for sport climbing.

routes.title: 15 Equipped Routes
routes.description: All routes have bolts already in place for safe climbing.

levels.title: Multiple Levels
levels.description: Routes of different difficulty levels for all climbers.

routes.title: Climbing Routes
routes.subtitle: All routes are equipped with bolted anchors.

guide.title: Route Map
guide.subtitle: Check the visual guide with the location and numbering of all Bendito Sea wall routes. You can enlarge it or download it to take with you.
guide.imageAlt: Route guide for the Bendito Sea wall

location.title: Where to find the wall?
location.p1: The Bendito Sea wall is within the Camping El Higuerón grounds, in the middle of the high Andean forest. Its privileged location lets you enjoy climbing while surrounded by an impressive natural landscape.
location.p2: From the camping area, access to the wall is straightforward and signposted. We recommend checking with our team for precise directions and the day's conditions.
location.imageAlt: Location of the Bendito Sea wall

safety.title: Safety Recommendations
safety.intro: Although the Bendito Sea wall is equipped with bolted anchors, climbing remains a risky activity. Every climber must take responsibility for their own safety.
tips: Always climb with a trusted partner
Check your gear before every attempt
Know your limits and respect them
Always wear a helmet in the area
Check the condition of the bolts before clipping
Respect the site guidelines

MBS01.description: It starts right where a tree is. It is to the left of Pioneros and is a good option for warming up.
tips: Located to the left of the Pioneros route
Excellent option for warming up before harder routes
Starts near a distinctive tree

MBS02.description: A sequence of beautiful moves with hand jugs that don't allow rest until the end once you enter the crux.
tips: Requires good hand-jug technique
Few rests: keep your pace and focus
The crux is intense but beautiful

MBS03.description: A simple start until you reach the overhang. Then it's pure crux on small holds and a really long move that may need a dynamic jump for shorter climbers.
tips: Accessible start but the crux is challenging
Very small holds on the overhang
A long, powerful move is required
Shorter climbers may need a dynamic move

MBS04.description: An easy route on the obvious line of easy progression between La Niebla and Perdidos en el Bosque. It starts on Perdidos en el Bosque, then trends slightly left onto the favorable slab, joins La Niebla, and finishes at a lower-off on the first ledge right where the high crack of Pioneros begins.
tips: Located on a natural progression of difficulty
Connects with two other important routes
Finishes at a well-defined lower-off
A good option for climbers in progression

MBS05.description: With the first bolt right beside you, there is a small crux reaching the second bolt. After that, good holds and very good feet. The move to the anchor defines the 5.10a.
tips: First bolt is well placed to start
Small crux in the first meters
Good holds and feet in the middle section
The final move defines the difficulty

MBS06.description: A long journey of many powerful sections on a slightly overhanging wall. A wide range of technical moves and a lot of endurance. Probably the hardest line in the sector so far.
tips: One of the most challenging routes on the wall
Multiple technical sections require focus
Excellent endurance is needed
Overhanging wall requires power and technique
Project - not fully established yet

MBS07.description: The first line in the park, a beautiful overhanging line. It gets harder as you go up, progressively increasing the grade. The line stays dry most of the time. Only a strong storm might wet the last bolt.
tips: The first line equipped on the wall
A beautiful, well-formed line
Progressively increases in difficulty
Generally dry except in heavy rain
Excellent for getting familiar with the wall

MBS08.description: A powerful boulder-style start with small holds and high feet. Followed by a small roof with long moves. Followed by a slippery section full of crimps. On the overhang, stay left for an overhanging section of long moves and good holds. Lots of endurance to a crimpy finish.
tips: Powerful boulder start - take time to warm up!
Small holds require fine technique
Technical roof with long moves
Slippery crimp section - watch your feet
The left side of the overhang has good holds
Excellent endurance is required to the end

MBS09.description: The line has 4 sections, each with its own small crux. There is a full rest zone in the middle of the line. Clipping the bolt before the anchor is scary but totally safe. The anchor and the last bolt get wet in heavy rain.
tips: Route named after the wall - very meaningful
Four distinct sections each with its own crux
Important rest in the middle of the route
The pre-anchor bolt inspires confidence - it's totally safe!
Last section may be wet after rain
Exceptional technique and endurance are required

MBS10.description: A mixed line, a gentle start through some bolts and an interesting final move on the rocky wall, where you need to place some nut protection to reach the anchor on the left.
tips: Mixed route: combines sport and traditional
Easy start with good bolts
Nut protection is required in the final section
Technical and interesting final move
A good introduction to mixed climbing
Anchor is to the left of the wall

MBS11.description: The start is an ocean of good holds and sandy cookies until you reach a move that requires pure balance and raising your feet very high. You need to make the move to clip — a very nice leap of faith.
tips: Start with good holds and sandy cookies
The crux requires pure balance
Raise your feet very high for the key move
You need to make the move to be able to clip
A beautiful leap of faith defines the route

MBS12.description: It starts with an overhang with good side pulls, crosses a crimp section, and progresses to the lava holds. The second half is an overhang with excellent holds.
tips: Initial overhang with good side pulls
Crimp section requires fine technique
Progresses toward unique lava holds
Second half is also overhanging
Excellent holds on the final part

MBS13.description: Mixed line. It starts with 6 bolts using side-pull technique. Climb to the ledge into a slap crux. Then work your way with nut protection through the second half across the rocky wall to a final bolt and an anchor at the end.
tips: First 6 bolts require side-pull technique
Crux is in the slap after the ledge
Second half requires nut protection (gear)
Traditional protection gear is needed
Finishes with a final bolt and anchor
Excellent introduction to mixed climbing

MBS14.description: A short, slippery 5.9 to the first anchor. Traverse left to reach an overhang and keep your endurance for some nice technical moves with good holds in the second half.
tips: Short 5.9 start as a warm-up
Initial section can be slippery
Traverse left for the overhang
Keep endurance for the second half
Nice technical moves up high
Good holds on the final part

MBS15.description: A route whose first section offers friendly, short, and easy sport climbing (5.9). After its first belay there is a mixed extension that follows the obvious thin crack requiring small protection until its second anchor. The difficulty of this second part could be around 5.11-.
tips: Easy sport first section - good warm-up
Second part is mixed/traditional climbing
Thin crack requires small protection
Traditional protection gear is needed
Second part significantly harder (5.11-)
Excellent for learning mixed climbing
